findings.issue: The correction plan matches a correction row to an earlier chain row by applicant key alone. In a valid several-rows-per-applicant batch (B14 accepts this pattern), every applicant key belongs to one row per service. Every correction row for such an applicant therefore gets two or more hits and becomes a false 'identity_conflict_in_batch' incident. No correction upload can ever correct or confirm these applicants. Even an identical re-upload opens new open intake incidents, which then also hold group closure.
findings.scenario: A TA bulk-uploads a sheet where applicant S5910001 has two rows (tourist eVisa, paper return) and S5910002 has one row. The attempt is fully_processed with row_pattern multiple_rows_per_applicant and all rows accepted. The TA uploads the identical file as a correction. Both rows of S5910001 become incident_open / identity_conflict_in_batch / unmatched, and two open ambiguous_applicant intake incidents appear. A real change to either row gives the same result.
findings.evidence: Ran a throwaway probe in test/intake against kit.bulkExcel and kit.correct. Output: MULTI FIRST fully_processed multiple_rows_per_applicant [accepted, accepted, accepted]. MULTI CORR [[incident_open, identity_conflict_in_batch, unmatched], [incident_open, identity_conflict_in_batch, unmatched], [untouched_by_correction, null, unchanged]]. MULTI INCIDENTS: 2 open ambiguous_applicant. Code: planCorrection 'if (hits.length > 1) return { ... state: incident_open, code: identity_conflict_in_batch }'. byKey groups chain rows by applicantKey only.
findings.fix: When the chain's row pattern is multiple_rows_per_applicant, match by applicant key plus service set (or applicant key plus original locator). Raise identity_conflict_in_batch only when the rows that share a key also differ in identity. Add a correction test for a several-rows-per-applicant chain.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced at 6360420. planCorrection groups chain rows by applicantKey only. More than one hit becomes unmatched / incident_open / identity_conflict_in_batch. A valid multiple_rows_per_applicant chain has one row per service for each repeated key, so every correction row for that applicant takes this branch. Design step 1 states the rule literally but ignores this pattern. That conflicts with the

findings.issue: An eligible per-service failure is never retried when another service in the same row succeeded. classify() treats a row as failed only when its state is failed/incident_open and it has no effect. A row with one created draft and one service refused for an eligible reason (for example offering_suspended, which is listed in ELIGIBLE_FAILURES) has state 'accepted'. An identical correction therefore classifies it 'unchanged' and never processes the refused service again. B16 requires that the Nth identical retry resolves accepted effects and eligible failures. A fresh bulk intake of the same file is refused with source_already_ingested, so the TA cannot retry from the same source either.
findings.scenario: Row 'S5900001, services: syn_paper_return, syn_tourist_evisa'. The paper offering is suspended while the attempt runs: tourist is created and paper is refused with offering_suspended (an eligible failure). The suspension ends. The TA uploads the identical sheet twice as corrections: each time the row is untouched_by_correction / unchanged with no service results, and only the tourist draft exists. Re-starting the same source is refused with conflict_duplicate source_already_ingested.
findings.evidence: Ran a throwaway probe in test/intake. Output: FIRST row accepted [paper: refused offering_suspended, tourist: created]. CORR row 0 untouched_by_correction unchanged []. CORR row 1 untouched_by_correction unchanged []. APPS [[tourist, draft]]. A new kit.bulkExcel of the same workbook was rejected: source_already_ingested. Code: 'const failed = FAILED_STATES.has(t.state) && !t.hasEffect' and 'if (same && !failed) return { cls: unchanged, state: untouched_by_correction }'.
findings.fix: Classify per service rather than per row. When the latest chain row has any service refused with an ELIGIBLE_FAILURES code and no effect for that offering, send the row on as failed_retry for those offerings only. acceptRow already resolves the created services through recorded effects, so no duplicate is created. Add a test with a partially refused row and an identical correction.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced at 6360420, and the defect is wider than the finding says. Partial rows: one created draft makes the row 'accepted' (rows.ts:220), so classify() calls an identical row 'unchanged'. Single-service rows: process-rows.ts:223 always stores row state_code = null for service refusals. A row refused only for offering_suspended is therefore 'failed' with code null, and classify (correction.ts:5

findings.issue: Document evidence changes are applied immediately while filing may have occurred. Field and identity corrections are held. Documents commands (upload, replace, associate, revoke) go through Core's 'correct_application' controls. Stage 8 for correct_application refuses only after evidenced filing or packet release. Nothing holds or refuses a document change while an act is 'authorized' or 'filing_unknown'. B23 requires proposed corrections to be held separately while filing is unknown. B19 requires protected facts to stay historical with no latest-write-wins. The evidence set that may have reached the authority is therefore changed in place.
findings.scenario: An operator authorizes a government submission (act 'authorized'), then formally returns the case to the TA. The TA's field edit is correctly held (held_filing_unknown). In the same state, the TA uploads a new photo and a new passport through doc.upload_for_application. Both are accepted: the new photo association becomes positive beside the original, and the new passport association is 'ambiguous' beside the filed one. The application's evidence state, fingerprint and requirement status change while filing is uncertain.
findings.evidence: Ran a throwaway probe in test/core using kit.submitted, ready, authorizeExternalAct, formalReturn and kit.upload. Output: ACT [authorized]. PHOTO UPLOAD accepted (status proposed). PASSPORT UPLOAD accepted. ASSOC AFTER adds {photo: positive} and {passport: ambiguous} to the two original positives. CORRECTIONS shows no held row for the document changes. Code: controls.ts stage 8 'else if (action === correct_application) { if (!open || filedEvidenced(acts) || packetRelease) push(correction_historical_after_filing) }'. There is no authorized/filing_unknown branch. documents/commands/associate.ts:64 relies on that evaluation.
findings.fix: When any act is 'authorized' or 'filing_unknown', refuse Documents association changes for the application with a filing_uncertainty_protection blocker (for example 'filing_possibly_occurred'), or hold them like the 3.2.1 correction rows. Release them through the same not_filed_evidenced / filed_evidenced resolution. Add a test next to the held-correction test in test/core/acts.test.ts.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced, and worse than reported. While a government_submission act is 'authorized', the TA can do three things after a formal return. The TA can upload a new photo and a new passport, and can revoke the passport association that was authorized for filing. Field edits in the same state are held, so only fields are protected. The spec says to protect attempted facts as if filed and to hold corre

findings.issue: core.link_dependency runs no control evaluation. It does not check for a protection mark or filing-uncertainty or filed acts, so a TA can add a declared dependency to an application that is filed or possibly filed (for example after a formal return) and bump its material revision. core.unlink_dependency refuses unless the case is confirmed unfiled, so the two commands disagree.
findings.scenario: A case is filed_evidenced, then the operator formally returns it to the TA. The TA links a new declared dependency. The link is accepted, material_revision increases, and the filed application gains a new prerequisite.
findings.evidence: Code reading: linkDependency handle checks only lifecycle open, taEditorPermits, the declared relation, outcome compatibility and cycles, and never calls requireControls. unlinkDependency has 'if (!confirmedUnfiled(await authorizationsOf(...))) throw filing_possibly_occurred'. No probe run.
findings.fix: Apply the same confirmedUnfiled / protection-mark check to link_dependency, or route it through requireControls with a correct_application-like stage 3 and stage 8.

findings.issue: In the three-instance topology a TA (or staff) byte retrieval is recorded as 'streamed' (TA page: 'Received') when the browser received nothing or only part of the file. Core records the result once it hands the bytes to its own socket toward edge. Edge's sendBytes pipes core's response into the browser reply, but a browser disconnect does not travel back to core. Design test T-15-33 requires 'client abort: stream_failed, never streamed'. Today that test runs only against core in a single process, so the traceability row says 'proven' while the deployed topology violates it.
findings.scenario: A TA's browser drops the connection after the download headers. Core has already written the file to its socket toward edge and records 'streamed' with the full size; the TA page shows 'Received'. For a packet, dlv.record_handover treats any 'streamed' packet release as system verification (handover.ts:93-97). With handover evidence ta_retrieval_of_released_packet, Core then records the preparation-only outcome 'prepared_and_handed_over' from a retrieval the TA never got. The ZIP selection ('included' per item), the SuperAdmin download and the review copy share this path.
findings.evidence: Ran a throwaway system probe (startThreeInstances, synthetic seed, TA1 application with accepted Passport and Photo). It posted the edge retrieval form, read only the status and headers, and destroyed the socket. Output: 'abortAfter=0 status=200 clientGot=0 size=1049 rows=[{"result":"streamed","b":1049}]'. The client received 0 bytes and core recorded streamed with 1049 bytes. Code: retrieval.ts:198 records 'streamed' when the core-side stream completes ('handed to the connection'). server.ts:431-462 does r.stream.pipe(check) and never reports the browser-side result to core. pages.ts:137 labels streamed 'Received'. test/delivery/release.test.ts:286 (T-15-33) covers only the kit, not the edge leg.
findings.fix: Make 'streamed' mean the end client received the bytes. Core keeps the result open until edge reports, through a send-end continuation under the same operation key, how the browser leg ended. Edge reports stream_failed on an early close. With no report, the result stays unrecorded. Alternatively, propagate the abort upstream and record only after edge acknowledges. Add a three-instance test that aborts a file, a ZIP and a packet after the headers and asserts no 'streamed' and no system-verified handover.

verdicts.reasoning: Real, but the probe overstates it. Fastify destroys only edge's `check` Transform, so core's response is never destroyed. Core reports complete on its own 'finish', meaning handed to the socket toward edge. A browser that aborts mid-stream, with the rest of the file still fitting in the buffers between core and edge, gets 'streamed' with the full size. A larger remainder is recorded as stream_fail

findings.issue: The completion check accepts any 'result_available' notice of the application as the web-notification evidence. The notice does not have to name the artifact version that the accepted email carried. This check runs only under the labelled harness, because the completion trigger is unselected (B46).
findings.scenario: A result notice is posted for artifact A. A is later replaced by artifact B, for example after a wrong-recipient block. An accepted email carries B. The harness completion check then counts the old notice for A as the web notification for B, so completion is satisfied without a notice about the delivered result.
findings.evidence: derived.ts:207-208: the email check matches artifactVersion, but the notice check is ev.notices.find((n) => n.kind === 'result_available') with no artifact or version match. evidence.ts:16-27 returns notices without params.
findings.fix: Require the notice params to name the eligible artifact (or its outcome) that the accepted email carried. Alternatively, record this as part of the B46 owner decision on the send event.

findings.issue: cat.approve_transition accepts any evidence entry of kind release_manifest as engineering compatibility evidence. It never checks that the id is a registered release or that it names the target binding. The contract (C14 check 5) requires 'a release_manifest evidence naming the target binding'. B06 requires engineering compatibility evidence for a per-application structural transition, so a SuperAdmin can supply that evidence alone by typing a label.
findings.scenario: A SuperAdmin publishes an owner-approved declaration on a launched offering. No release impact statement exists, so `named` is null. The SuperAdmin approves the transition of a draft with compatibilityEvidence [{kind:'release_manifest', id:'compat-1'}]. 'compat-1' is not a release and names no binding. The transition is accepted, and the draft's governing tuple moves to the new head at once. A submitted application gets the same acceptance and only waits for TA authority.
findings.evidence: impact.ts:218 `const manifestEvidence = input.compatibilityEvidence.some((e) => e.kind === 'release_manifest');` is the only check. No lookup of the release or the binding id follows. Reproduced: test/integration/catalogue-impact.test.ts 'a submitted application with a material difference waits for renewed travel agent authority; a draft transitions at once' passes with ids 'compat-1' and 'compat-2' (3/3 pass in this worktree). The draft's declaration_id became the new head.
findings.fix: Accept release_manifest evidence only when its id equals a registered release that supports the head binding (bindingStatus(head.bindingId, thatRelease) = 'supported'), or when the evidence names head.bindingId. Otherwise refuse with transition_evidence_missing. Add a negative test that uses an unknown release id.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Check 5 of record 12 requires a statement that says requires_transition or compatible_continuation. Otherwise the input must carry a release_manifest evidence naming the target binding. The code only checks the kind, so a free-typed id passes. No override or parked item covers this. I rank it P1, not P0. The handler already refuses unless the head binding is 'supported' by the running r

findings.issue: After a group travel-date edit, the core.travel_date_recheck task re-reads only document validity. It never calls catalogue.evaluateTravelDateRules (the declared travel-date rules and the country adapter checks, which get the `submitted` flag). It then always advances dates_checked_revision, which clears travel_date_recheck_pending. Record 12 §2.6 and T-C23 require Core to recheck with evaluateTravelDateRules and to keep travel_date_recheck_pending while the validity is unknown. For submitted applications, no other code path evaluates the travel rules: stage 10 runs them only for 'submit', with submitted:false.
findings.scenario: Take an offering whose declaration names a country_adapter_check with fn evaluateTravelDateRules, where the adapter judges submitted work. The TA moves the group's travel start earlier. The recheck task marks the submitted, unfiled application as checked. This holds when the adapter would answer invalid, and also when it throws or overruns, which should give unknown and a country_defect. Readiness and filing authorization then proceed with no travel-date blocker. The catalogue impact recheck (impact-recheck.ts:114) does evaluate the same rules with submitted:true for a catalogue change, so the two recheck paths judge the same application differently.
findings.evidence: tasks.ts:177-198: the record step computes codes only from documents.requirementEvidence, then runs `UPDATE core_applications SET dates_checked_revision = ${group.dates_revision}` without a condition. No call to deps.catalogue.evaluateTravelDateRules exists outside controls.ts:532 (the submit branch of validationStage). No test asserts travel_date_recheck_pending (grep over test/ finds none). The groups-drafts test asserts only that the revision advances.
findings.fix: In the recheck record step, for unfiled, unprotected applications, call deps.catalogue.evaluateTravelDateRules(governing declaration, governing baseline, {travel dates, today, submitted: lifecycle === 'submitted'}) inside the adapter boundary. Record its codes. Leave dates_checked_revision unchanged (keep the blocker) while validity is 'unknown', and surface 'invalid' as a stage-10 blocker. Add the T-C23 test: unknown or adapter failure keeps travel_date_recheck_pending, and filed facts stay unchanged.

At 6360420 the core.travel_date_recheck record step (tasks.ts:168-198) re-reads only documents.requirementEvidence, then advances dates_checked_revision unconditionally. evaluateTravelDateRules runs only at submit (controls.ts:532, submitted:false) and in the catalogue impact recheck (impact-recheck.ts:114). findings.issue: The operator surface has no country/service discovery. B01 requires operator/SuperAdmin surfaces with country/service discovery. Record 12 §5 designs a read-only operator route `/ops/catalogue/offerings/:offeringId` (catalogue.read_selectable). The route inventory and the staff app do not implement it, and no recorded gap or visible unavailable state replaces it. The policy grants operators catalogue.read_selectable, but no route uses that grant for operators.
findings.scenario: An operator signs in to the staff instance. findings.issue: Incident access through the owner or reviewer relation outlives reassignment. transferApplicationDuties moves only incidents in state open, assigned or awaiting_evidence. The 'asg_or_rev' relation (policy.ts:553-556) grants incident.read, incident.work and incident.resolve to whoever is still stored as owner or reviewer. It checks neither the incident state nor current assignment. So the former operator keeps the old link to a resolved or closed incident and can still run ops.close_incident. The review-copy relation (reviewArtifact) already limits itself to open incidents; this relation does not.
findings.scenario: Op1 is assigned to TA1's application. Op1 opens an operational_failure incident whose note contains the applicant's name and passport number, then resolves it. A SuperAdmin reassigns the application to op2. After that, op1 gets 404 on /ops/applications/<app>, which is correct. But GET /ops/incidents/<inc> still returns 200, with the note, the resolution, the evidence references and the application reference. POST /ops/incidents/<inc>/close is accepted (303), and the row records closed_by = op1. The closed incident stays readable to op1 indefinitely. The same root cause applies to a stand-in reviewer: when the case is later assigned, the reviewer keeps resolved incidents.
findings.evidence: Probe on the three instances (throwaway system test, not committed). The incident row before and after reassignment was {state: resolved, owner_kind: assigned_operator, owner_account_id: op1}, so it was not transferred. After reassignment: op1 case page 404, op2 case page 200, op1 incident page 200 showing the applicant marker, the passport number and the application id. The op1 close returned 303 and the row became {state: closed, closed_by: op1}. Afterwards op1 could still read the closed incident (200). Code: incidents.ts:222 limits the transfer to open states. policy.ts:497-504 resolves the incident owner and reviewer without the state. policy.ts:553-556 honours them unconditionally. Bounded impact: a resolved incident's content no longer changes, and the only action left is close.
findings.fix: Make the owner and reviewer relation hold only while the incident is open, and only while the owner is still the application's current assigned operator (or the incident has no application). Mirror the 'about' rule of reviewArtifact. Also transfer resolved, not-yet-closed incidents in transferApplicationDuties. Add a system test: reassign, then the former operator gets 404 on the incident page and on close.

findings.issue: The fetch worker's IPv6 deny list does not include the deprecated IPv4-compatible block ::/96. ipaddr.js classifies hex-form addresses such as ::7f00:1 (127.0.0.1) and ::a00:1 (10.0.0.1) as 'unicast'. Both isPublicAddress and the request-filtering-agent connect-time check therefore accept them. This contradicts the file's statement that embedded IPv4 forms are denied outright.
findings.scenario: A travel agent's row-file link names a host whose DNS gives only the AAAA answer ::7f00:1. checkAddresses accepts it, the pinned lookup connects to it, and RequestFilteringHttpsAgent also accepts it. The request reaches loopback only on a host whose kernel still routes IPv4-compatible addresses, for example through a legacy sit0 automatic tunnel. On this host the connection does not complete. Low likelihood.
findings.evidence: node probe: isPublicAddress('::7f00:1') = true, isPublicAddress('::a00:1') = true. ipaddr.parse('::7f00:1').range() = 'unicast'. request-filtering-agent allows range 'unicast' (lib line 80). On this host a connect to ::7f00:1 with a listener on 127.0.0.1 did not complete.
findings.fix: Add '::/96' to DENY_V6, keeping ::/128 and ::1/128, or deny any IPv6 address whose first 96 bits are zero. Add the case to the SSRF unit tests.

findings.issue: A transport failure between core and edge's processing service (edge restart, 503 on stop, or health already marked down) is recorded as a fact about the file, not as a retryable outage. In doc.parse, extract() catches every worker-job exception and returns a tool-failure finding, so the version settles as extraction_failed (extraction_tool_failed). Intake has the same class: fetchToStaging turns transport worker_failed into an outcome, and fetch-row-files records the link as 'unreadable' without retry. Also, the compose flag scannerUp updates only on the 10 s probe, so scan tasks are still leased after a markDown and spend scanner_unavailable counts.
findings.scenario: Edge restarts while parse tasks are in flight. One OCR job fails in transport and markDown() clears the health. Every other in-flight task past inspect_pdf then gets worker_failed at once and settles as extraction_failed. A passport then needs a manual TA resolution or a SuperAdmin requeue. An official result opens an association incident (extraction_unavailable). Because the listener returns early once incident_id is set, a later requeue never restores automatic association. Bulk row files fetched during the restart are recorded as unreadable links, and the drafts are created without them.
findings.evidence: Probe: parseEffect with inspect_pdf ok, then the next job throws TmError('unavailable_dependency','worker_failed'), as processing-client post() does on a transport error. Output: jobs [inspect_pdf, extract_pdf_text]; result {kind:'passed', finding:{toolFailed:true}, failureCode:'worker_failed'}; decision 'failed extraction_tool_failed -> extraction_failed'. Code: parse.ts:127-131 (catch-all); processing-client.ts post() and run(); association.ts early return on incident_id; fetch-source.ts:66-68; fetch-row-files.ts record (no RETRYABLE_FETCH rethrow, unlike fetch-source); compose.ts:770 (scannerUp).
findings.fix: Give processing-client transport and health failures a distinct code, for example processing_unreachable. extract(), the row-file fetch and scanEffect MUST rethrow it, so the task retries and facility gating stops leases. Only a worker's own response MAY become an extraction or link verdict. The scanner facility SHOULD follow the client health at once. Add a system test that restarts edge mid-parse and mid-fetch.

findings.issue: The periodic enqueue jobs select with ORDER BY id LIMIT and keep no cursor, while their task dedupe keys are per day. Rows that never leave the selection therefore hold the window permanently. group_end_enqueue takes the first 500 open groups past their return date. A group with any paid or worked case never closes, because in production nothing leaves lifecycle 'submitted': completion is harness-only. timing_risk_enqueue takes the first 1000 submitted applications with no outcome, and cases that wait on filing_unknown, deferral or an external result stay in that set.

Their unpaid, unworked drafts (including withdrawn ones) never end with the group, and the group never closes, which violates the group-end rule. Once more than 1000 submitted applications without an outcome exist across all travel agents, newer applications never get the daily elapsed-window or travel-start timing check, so their timing notice is never posted.

findings.issue: Association rule assoc/1 walks openApplicationsForOffering: every draft or submitted application of the offering for all travel agents, in id order. It stops silently after 2000 rows (CANDIDATE_LIMIT) and then decides as if the walk were complete. Worked applications never leave 'submitted' in production, so the open set of an offering grows without bound. Once past 2000, the newest applications, which receive the results, lie beyond the window. Rule 3 (exactly one candidate) and rule 6 (no contradictory identifier) are then evaluated on a partial set.
findings.scenario: An offering has more than 2000 submitted applications. (a) Each new result is uploaded for an application beyond the window, fails with no_candidate and opens an incident, so automatic association is in effect disabled. (b) A travel agent has the same applicant in two filed groups of the offering. Trip 2's visa is uploaded to the trip-1 application, which lies inside the window, while the trip-2 application lies beyond it. Only one candidate is seen, and the visa is verified and released for the wrong trip without the required conflict review.
findings.evidence: Code: association.ts:52-53 and 81-96 (10 pages of 200; no truncation signal; the decision at 98-100 treats the partial walk as complete). catalogue-writers.ts:69-73: lifecycle IN ('draft','submitted') for all travel agents, ORDER BY application_id. admin.ts:209 is the only writer of 'completed' (harness). The exported OPEN_INCIDENT_STATES (store.ts:167) is not imported by any of these. The blocking-kind rule has three forms: the unused export BLOCKING_KINDS (incidents.ts:35), the SQL literal in blockingIncidents (incidents.ts:202) and an inline copy in delivery/pages.ts:116.
findings.scenario: An engineer reads BLOCKING_KINDS ('Kinds that block a byte release') and adds a kind there. Nothing changes, because the byte-release gate uses the SQL literal at line 202. The opposite case also fails silently: a new blocking kind or open state is added to the SQL gate, but delivery/pages.ts still computes applicationBlocked from its own copy. The TA delivery page then shows no block while release refuses.
findings.evidence: incidents.ts:35 BLOCKING_KINDS has no reference outside its file (unused-export scan). incidents.ts:202 has kind IN ('wrong_recipient_disclosure', 'bytes_integrity'). delivery/pages.ts:115-116 repeats both the state set and the kind set inline.
findings.fix: Add OPEN_OPS_INCIDENT_STATES and BLOCKING_OPS_INCIDENT_KINDS to src/kernel/vocabulary/incidents.ts, where BFFs can also load them. Bind the arrays into the SQL (= ANY(...)) and use them in delivery and the staff BFF. Delete the dead export.

findings.issue: Production code and tests never call these exported symbols, and several look authoritative. controls.ts:713-731: canSubmit, canAssign, canStartOperatorWork, canAuthorizeFiling, canReleasePacket and canSelectOffering. errors.ts:160 notImplemented. retry.ts:30 isConnectionLevelError. recovery.ts:325 lastCompleteBackup, which compose.ts:773 and capacity.ts:275 duplicate. delivery: releaseUnrecorded, readPacketsOf. catalogueCommandList. intake: fileSettled, TERMINAL_STATES, TERMINAL_ROW_STATES. core/store.ts: readSnapshot, readAssistance, assignmentsOf, readAuthorization, bumpApplication. NO_SESSIONS. Staff catalogue intField.
findings.scenario: An onboarding engineer adds a new submit-time control and changes canSubmit or TERMINAL_STATES, expecting a behaviour change. Nothing changes, and the engineer loses time or merges a no-op believed to be a fix.
findings.evidence: A TypeScript AST scan (scratchpad unused.mjs) flagged each name as declared once and referenced nowhere else in src, test, scripts or catalogue. Spot-checks confirmed the results by grep.
findings.fix: Delete the listed symbols. If useful, add an unused-export check (for example a small TS scan in test/static) that skips the closed-vocabulary z*/type exports.

findings.issue: The architecture layer table says the Web layer (src/web) 'May import kernel, platform, module api.ts'. The service split forbids this. Edge and staff load src/web, and app-boundary.ts forbids every src/modules/ file for a BFF, including api.ts. The section 'Case work, delivery and views: who owns which files' describes the milestone-4 parallel build ('frozen interfaces', 'append-only shared files') in the present tense, but that process has ended. frozen-interfaces.test.ts still pins exact function lists.
findings.scenario: An onboarding engineer follows the table and imports a module's api.ts from a src/web helper. The service-split static test fails with an app_imports_domain path that the documentation said was allowed. Another engineer reads the append-only and frozen-interface rules as current policy and avoids a valid refactor of src/contracts/delivery.ts.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture.md layer table, Web row; test/static/lib/app-boundary.ts APP_FORBIDDEN includes /^src\/modules\//; src/web contains no module import (grep), which shows that the documented permission is unused.
findings.fix: Change the Web row to 'kernel vocabulary and pure helpers, platform TLS/config, contracts; never modules'. Rewrite the ownership section as historical, or remove it, and keep the composition-port paragraph.

findings.issue: Some modules read other modules' tables directly with SQL, and no static test covers these reads. Core reads cat_countries and cat_offerings (lists.ts:31,68,124,145; staff-views.ts:181; catalogue-reads.ts). Intake reads cat_countries (planning.ts:175). Delivery reads core_packet_releases (packets.ts:113). The identity policy reads core_applications.assigned_operator_id (policy.ts:730,737). The sole-writers static test checks only writes, so these reads break only at runtime. core/catalogue-reads.ts records itself as debt.
findings.scenario: Catalogue renames or splits cat_countries.name, or Core moves the operator assignment into its own table. Type checking and the static tests pass. Core's group lists and Intake planning then fail at runtime with a SQL error, and the identity policy's group.read and incident.read scope predicates fail as well. Only tests that exercise those paths catch the failure.
findings.evidence: A grep of FROM/JOIN across src/modules/* found these foreign-prefix reads. test/static/lib/sole-writers.ts header: 'each module is the only writer'; it has no read rule.
findings.fix: Expose the reads through the owners' api.ts queries (the catalogue country query and Core's operator-of-application). Alternatively, list the accepted cross-owner reads in a static allowlist so that a new one is a reviewed decision.

findings.issue: composeDomain is one function of about 370 lines (compose.ts:545-914, 50 KB file). It wires every module, owns the timers and probes, builds health and the backup-age check, and handles shutdown and undo. It re-implements kernel queries (backup age at compose.ts:773). The test suite (1698 tests, 414 s) is dominated by two 50-iteration race loops: payments/exposure.test.ts 'concurrent commitments ... (50 races)' takes 96.5 s and the correction/assignment race takes 29 s.
findings.scenario: A change to health or probe behaviour has to be made inside the single wiring function, where an accidental change to the undo order or timer cancellation is easy to miss in review. Separately, a developer running one test file waits about 100 s for one race test.
findings.evidence: Function outline of src/domain/compose.ts. The TAP durations from a full run in the throwaway worktree: tests 1698, pass 1698, skipped 0, duration_ms 414358.
findings.fix: Move health and probes and the job/timer set into their own composition files that return cancel handles. Use the kernel query. Make the race-loop count an environment knob, for example 10 by default and 50 in a full check.

findings.issue: Declared travel-date rules (eligibility.travelDateRules and evaluateTravelDateRules adapter checks) run only when controls.submitChecks lists travel_dates_valid. Nothing requires that opt-in: the parser accepts a travel-date adapter check without it. The synthetic declarations omit it, so the seeded SYX check syx_min_lead_days never runs at submit. No test uses it and the guides never mention it. Readiness and the date-change recheck never evaluate travel rules. Yet the declaration page lists travel date rules as Supported, Launch required, gating submit and record_readiness.
findings.scenario: SYZ onboarded through the documented pages with country_adapter_check syz.core@1.0.0 evaluateTravelDateRules syz_max_stay_days {days:30} and the usual submitChecks [mandatory_documents_present, identity_evidence_present]. A travel agent creates an SYZ group from today+30 to today+75 (46 days) and submits a complete draft. The submission is accepted, so the application goes to filing in breach of the declared country rule. Add travel_dates_valid and the same draft is refused. A misconfiguration the guides invite therefore fails open.
findings.evidence: Probe on three instances. Without travel_dates_valid, the long-stay submit answered 303 ?done=submitted. With it, the ready page showed 'The application cannot be submitted yet' and nothing was submitted, while the 11-day SYZ case still went through to delivery. controls.ts:527 `if (checks.includes('travel_dates_valid'))` is the only submit-time caller of evaluateTravelDateRules. core/tasks.ts travelDateRecheckTask re-reads document evidence only. `grep -r travel_dates_valid test/` finds nothing. The SYX submitChecks in catalogue.json omit it.
findings.fix: Fail closed. Either always evaluate declared travel rules and travel-date adapter checks at submit, or refuse a decl/1 body that declares them without travel_dates_valid. Add travel_dates_valid to the synthetic declarations. Add a system test for the invalid, unknown and valid cases. Document the rule in new-service.md.

findings.issue: The documented procedure does not work as written. (1) It omits the owner's structure approval (cat.record_owner_approval, approvalKind=structure). Without it the declaration stays draft and neither the baseline editor nor bind is offered; step 5 covers only gated items. (2) It omits cat.preview_declaration and cat.publish_declaration, the only step that sets the head. (3) Step 3's baseline 'preview then publish' is not offered for a new offering. (4) Launch must acknowledge the unresolved priceFeeRelation item, which contradicts 'no unsupported capability'. (5) A real offering's structure approval needs owner_approval evidence.
findings.scenario: A SuperAdmin follows new-service.md literally: offering, draft declaration, then step 3 'Baseline'. No baseline editor is shown. Step 4 'Bind': no bind form is shown. The service goes live only by guessing the undocumented order: structure approval, bind, baseline draft, declaration preview with that baseline, declaration publish, launch plan, launch with acknowledgements.
findings.evidence: Probe log. The doc-order baseline editor was not offered (false) and the doc-order bind was not offered (false). After the structure approval (303), the bind form appeared (303), the baseline draft was accepted (303) and the baseline page had no preview form. The declaration preview (303) and the declaration publish (303, pub_…?done=published) set the head. The launch form carried ack.financialConditions.priceFeeRelation. Both new applications then completed intake through edge delivery.
findings.fix: Rewrite the steps in the order the product enforces: offering; draft; structure approval (plus gated-item approvals); bind; baseline draft; declaration preview with that baseline; publish from the declaration page; launch plan; launch with acknowledgements. Fix 'Checks before launch'. Add a system test that onboards through the staff pages; none exists today.

findings.issue: After a declaration preview, staff redirects to /admin/catalogue/previews/:id. That page renders the baseline's 'Publish these values' form whenever the baseline is previewed under this preview id, and never checks preview.kind. For a declaration preview, that form always fails at core with preview_stale and the false message 'The work or the offering changed since the preview'. The form that works is on the declaration page. This affects every first publication of a new offering and every declaration change published with a new baseline.
findings.scenario: On a new offering, the SuperAdmin previews the declaration with its drafted baseline, lands on the preview page and clicks Publish. The answer is 409 preview_stale and nothing is published. Repeating the preview gives the same result, so the SuperAdmin is told the offering changed when it did not.
findings.evidence: Probe log: 'preview page forms' = ['/sign-out','/admin/catalogue/baselines/bbv_…/publish']. Submitting it gave 409 'Reference code: preview_stale'. The declaration page's /publish form then succeeded (303). baselines.ts:111 `const open = m.baseline !== null && m.baseline.status === 'previewed' && m.baseline.preview_id === m.preview.preview_id;`. commands/baselines.ts:152 refuses because preview.declaration_id !== head_declaration_id.
findings.fix: Show the baseline publish form only for preview.kind === 'baseline'. For a declaration preview, render the declaration publish form, or redirect the preview to the declaration page's publish section. Add a test that publishes a first declaration with its baseline through the pages.

findings.issue: Registering an adapter exactly as new-country.md says ('one entry … npm run check MUST pass') breaks npm run check. Tests outside the documented extension points pin the exact registry list. For a real ISO adapter, the production expectations also break, because those tests assert the production adapter set and capabilities are empty.
findings.scenario: Register syz.core (or a real fra.core) with one registry entry. Three tests fail: conformance.test.ts:10 and registry.test.ts:64-65 and :72. For a real adapter, registry.test.ts:66 activeAdapters('production').list() = [] and :68 adapterCapabilities('production') = [] fail too.
findings.evidence: Ran test/countries and test/static with SYZ registered: 109 tests, 3 fail (actual [... 'country.syz.core@1.0.0'] against an expected list of two). After those two test files were updated, the full suite passed: 1712 of 1712, the probe included.
findings.fix: Assert properties instead of the literal list: synthetic entries absent in production, every entry has a capability, and the reference adapters are present. Or name these files as a required step in new-country.md.

findings.issue: (1) The functions table implies the product uses proposeIntakeMapping and recognizeArtifact. Only checkValidity (validity.ts:140) and evaluateTravelDateRules (travel.ts:86) are invoked. Unused mapping is parked; unused recognition is not: official results are matched by the shared rule assoc/1 (case-work/association.ts). (2) The synthetic package location src/countries/synthetic/<code> (synthetic: true, non-ISO code), which the registry enforces, is undocumented. (3) The digest includes fixtures.ts but not the shared contract.ts (dayNumber, paramsSatisfy, schemas) that adapters import.
findings.scenario: An engineer implements recognizeArtifact for a new country so its grant numbers are recognised. The conformance kit passes, but the adapter is never called and results are still matched only by passport number and name. Separately, a fix to dayNumber in contract.ts changes the date verdicts of syn.core@1.0.0 for applications already bound to it, and the release registers without capability_digest_changed.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn invokeAdapter src` lists only validity.ts and travel.ts. registry.ts adapterSourceDigest hashes only entry.files under packageDir. registry.ts checkRegistry requires src/countries/synthetic/<code> for synthetic entries.
findings.fix: Mark proposeIntakeMapping and recognizeArtifact as not yet used by the product, or wire them in. Document the synthetic package location. Either cover contract.ts in every adapter digest, or treat any behavioural change to contract.ts as a new adapter API version.

findings.issue: Hard-coding inventory: no country, service or price rule is hard-coded in shared code beyond what the specification sanctions (TRAVEL_PURPOSES, IND). Remaining items: (a) the synthetic guards list only SYN and SYX (SYNTHETIC_MARKERS here; /^sy[nx]_/ in test/static/lib/code-literals.ts), and the literal scanner flags ISO codes only, so a shared-code branch on 'SYZ' or 'SYN' passes; (b) document-type labels in TYPE_OPTIONS (shared/pages/documents.ts:301, parked) and artifact-type labels humanized from codes; (c) 'passport' literals at controls.ts:514, decl.ts:468, originals.ts:113, parse.ts:253; (d) the baseline price field rejects '2,750'.
findings.scenario: A third synthetic country (code SYZ) in public content or shared code is not caught by the synthetic-content or literal guards. A SuperAdmin typing the price as the preview page shows it ('2,750') gets 422 'servicePricePaise: invalid format', an error that names an internal field.
findings.evidence: Probe: price '2,750' gave 422 'servicePricePaise: invalid format'; '2750.00' was accepted. Delivery pages showed 'Evisa grant (official result)'. read-models.ts:232 rupeesToPaise compared with shared/pages/payments.ts paiseFromRupees.
findings.fix: Derive synthetic markers from the registry or from is_synthetic codes, and flag any three-letter upper-case code literal outside src/countries. Add labels for declared artifact types to bv/1. Use one rupee parser for both forms.
